general_information.Description: This course offers an introduction to the fundamental principles of PR writing, with a specific focus on the influence of integrating artificial intelligence (AI). In the digital age, PR writing has evolved, using diverse channels such as blogs and social media. This evolution surpasses traditional press releases by incorporating the real-time nature of tweets, Instagram stories, LinkedIn posts, and the like. These versatile technologies enable a broad spectrum of approaches to PR writing and engagement, illustrating a noteworthy advancement in public relations techniques that are adept at navigating an ever-evolving communication environment. Upon successful completion of this course, students will acquire: 1. A comprehensive understanding of the transformative impact of digital spaces on information flow and knowledge acquisition, including the ability to distinguish between linear and non-linear media. 2. Proficiency in employing digital writing techniques to enhance readability and user engagement. 3. Mastery in editing for digital media to ensure accuracy and clarity, while adapting to the evolving roles of digital editors and content producers. 4. Ability to strategically utilize multimedia storytelling and public relations techniques, address legal considerations, and combat misinformation to maintain credibility and trust in digital journalism.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, questions, assignments given by instructor(s)/ lecturer(s) in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purposes - Promptly access to the FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Comprehend the transformative impacts of digital spaces on information flow and knowledge acquisition.
Employ various digital writing techniques effectively to enhance readability and user engagement.
Show proficiency in utilizing AI tools for error-free content and in editing digital media to ensure accuracy and clarity, adapting to the evolving roles of digital editors and content producers
Develop strategies utilizing multimedia storytelling and public relations techniques to achieve campaign objectives, while also addressing legal issues and combating misinformation.
Demonstrate professional and ethical conduct while working effectively, whether independently or in group collaborations.

assessments.Grading Guide: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions

assessments.Question Type: Suggested assignment requirement:Develop a comprehensive multimedia project aligned with your team's interests, such as addressing climate change. Your essay should:(a) Clearly state the chosen topic, outline specific project goals, define your target audience, and specify the types of multimedia content you plan to incorporate.(b) Explain your strategy for utilizing public relations techniques to expand the project's reach, address relevant legal and ethical issues, and propose methods for evaluating the project's impact on raising awareness or advocating for change related to your chosen topic.Notes:Students are required to:1. Use AI tools for text editing to enhance clarity and ensure the text is free of grammatical errors.2. Note that while AI tools may be used to edit content for digital media: • Students must acknowledge all AI-generated information in their reports. • Students must demonstrate their ability to produce content for digital media independently. • The use of AI tools is required but will not be graded separately; the quality of their completed work will be assessed as a whole.• The final assessment will be based on the lecturer's provided rubric.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Demonstrate the ability to produce content in diverse forms and genres across digital platforms, supported by strong writing and research skills.
assessments.Grading Guide: Grading Rubric – Group Assignment (Total: 100%) 1. Content & Project Design (30%) - Clear definition of topic, project goals, and target audience – 10% - Effective integration of multimedia elements appropriate to the topic – 10% - Depth of analysis with strong evidence and critical thinking – 10% 2. Strategy, Legal & Ethical Considerations (25%): - Well-developed PR strategy to maximize reach – 10% - Awareness of legal and ethical issues (copyright, misinformation, transparency) – 8% - Clear evaluation methods for measuring project impact – 7% 3. Application of AI (15%): - Effective use of AI for brainstorming, outlining, research, and drafting – 5% - AI-supported content creation (visuals, videos, PR drafts, proofreading) – 5% - Critical reflection on AI’s limitations, ethics, and responsible application – 5% 4. Writing Quality (10%): - Clear, coherent, and professional essay writing – 5% - Accuracy in grammar, spelling, and mechanics – 5% 5. Presentation & Delivery (20%): Well-structured and visually engaging slides – 5% Clear explanation about the usage of AI – 5% Confident, clear delivery with good pacing and teamwork – 5% Well answer all questions – 5%
assessments.Note: Students are strongly advised to carefully review all outputs from AI tools. They must demonstrate the ability to independently produce content for digital media. Students' work will be assessed according to a rubric provided by the lecturer. According to the predetermined LOs, lecturers have the flexibility to choose assignment forms. Each assignment has a six-day due date, which commences when the lecture provides detailed instructions.

assessments.Question Type: Individual Assignment 1: Students complete it at homeSuggested topic: (a) Select a news website or application and conduct an in-depth analysis to better understand its audience. Explore its FAQs and "About Us" section to determine its categorization (news, entertainment, reference, etc.), available content types, demographics of its visitors or subscribers (including age and education), content-related interests or needs addressed, and the nature of user engagement such as feedback, comments, and interaction. Utilizing this data, craft a user profile detailing the characteristics and behaviors of the site or app's audience.(b) Find an online news article that could be enhanced with an informative graphic, such as a chart or graph. Detail clear instructions for crafting this visual component, specifying the data to be included, the timeframe to be covered, and any additional features or dimensions necessary to aid the reader's comprehension of the story.Individual Assignment 2: In classWrite a short and engaging digital news story.Students choose a recent event (on or off campus).Write a short news story (maximum 200 words) designed for an online platform (e.g., news website or social media).Requirements:- Clear, concise, and shareable headline.- Opening paragraph answers the 5W1H (Who, What, Where, When, Why, How).- Language must be concise and appropriate for digital readers.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Evaluate the knowledge and skills students have developed during the course up to the time of the assignment
assessments.Grading Guide: Individual Assignment 1: Students complete it at home Grading Rubric (Total: 100%) - Content Accuracy & Relevance (25%): Analysis or article enhancement is accurate, comprehensive, and directly relevant to the task requirements. - Clarity, Grammar & Spelling (20%): Writing is polished, grammatically correct, and free from spelling errors. - Organization & Coherence (20%): Work is logically structured, flows smoothly, and demonstrates strong argumentation or explanation. - Critical Thinking & Insight (20%): Shows thoughtful analysis of audience characteristics or effective reasoning in designing the visual component; demonstrates originality and depth. - AI Application (15%): AI tools are applied effectively for research, idea generation, or editing. Outputs are properly acknowledged, critically evaluated, and meaningfully integrated with the student’s own work. Individual Assignment 2: In class Grading Rubric (Total: 100%) - Contextual Understanding – 20%: Comprehend the transformative impacts of digital spaces on information flow and knowledge acquisition. - Digital Writing Techniques – 30%: Employ various digital writing techniques effectively to enhance readability and user engagement. Assessing headline quality, 5W1H coverage, and concise language relates to mastering digital writing skills. - Accuracy and Clarity – 20%: Ensure accuracy and clarity in digital media editing and content production. - Structure and Expression – 10%: Employ various digital writing techniques effectively… - Grammar and Spelling – 10%: Ensure accuracy and clarity in digital media. - Professional and Ethical Conduct – 10%: Demonstrate professional and ethical conduct while working effectively, whether independently or in group collaborations.
assessments.Note: According to the predetermined LOs, lecturers have the flexibility to choose assignment forms. Individual assignment 1 has a six-day due date, which commences when the lecture provides detailed instructions. Students complete the individual assignment number 2 in class under lecturer supervision, without using any materials (including electronic resources).

assessments.Question Type: Essay Exam: The questions will cover selected material from lectures, class discussions, activities, exercises, and the textbook.

schedule.Topic: In-class Activity: Using AI for Editing Drafts Students will practice applying AI tools to enhance the quality of written content. This exercise focuses on developing editing skills by combining AI assistance with human judgment. Students will be provided with a short draft press release or blog post containing intentional grammatical, spelling, and stylistic errors. Using an AI editing tool, students must: - Edit the draft to correct grammar, spelling, and style. - Submit two deliverables: (1) The AI-edited version of the draft. (2) A brief reflection (approx. 150 words) explaining how the AI tool improved the text and identifying areas where human editing remained necessary.

schedule.Topic: In-class Activity: AI-Assisted Digital Writing Students will be assigned a short PR-related writing task (e.g., drafting a blog post, a LinkedIn update, or a news story for the website). Using an AI writing tool, students must: - Generate a first draft with AI assistance, based on the given prompt. - Revise and edit the draft to ensure clarity, accuracy, and appropriateness for the intended digital platform and target audience. - Submit two deliverables: (1) the unedited AI-generated draft, and (2) the polished final version revised by the student. Additionally, students will provide a 150–200 word reflection or oral statement explaining how AI contributed to the writing process and identifying areas where human intervention was essential.

schedule.Topic: In-class Activity: AI-Supported Fact-Checking and Editorial Response Students will be provided with two short online texts (e.g., news posts, blog excerpts, or social media updates), one containing reliable information and one containing misinformation. Using an AI tool, students must: - Analyze the texts and identify factual inaccuracies, biased language, or credibility issues. - Verify the information using AI fact-checking prompts and cross-referencing suggested sources. - Write a short editorial response (200–250 words) that corrects the misinformation, explains the risks it poses to public trust, and demonstrates professional PR writing style. - Submit both the AI analysis outputs and the final editorial response.
